paths.title: Start with the Greeks
paths.blurb: From fables to philosophy in seven books, roughly in the order they were written.

steps.title: Aesops Fables
steps.note: Short and easy, and a gentle first taste of the Greek way of telling a story with a point.

steps.title: The Iliad
steps.note: A few weeks in the tenth year of the Trojan War, and the anger of Achilles. Everything later in Greek literature looks back to it.

steps.title: The Odyssey
steps.note: Odysseus's long voyage home, and the most readable of the ancient epics.

steps.title: Anabasis
steps.note: A true adventure: ten thousand Greek soldiers stranded in Persia, told by one of their generals.

steps.title: The Republic
steps.note: Socrates asks what justice is, and builds an ideal city to find out.

steps.title: Nicomachean Ethics
steps.note: Aristotle on happiness, virtue and friendship. Slower going, but it repays the effort.

steps.title: Plutarchs Lives
steps.note: Dip in anywhere: lives of famous Greeks and Romans, side by side.

paths.title: Rome in Its Own Words
paths.blurb: Soldiers, statesmen, poets and philosophers: Rome from the late Republic to its fall.

steps.title: The Gallic War
steps.note: Caesar's own report of his conquest of Gaul, in clear, plain prose.

steps.title: On Duties
steps.note: One of Cicero's last books, written for his son in the year Caesar was killed: how to live honourably.

steps.title: The Early History Of Rome
steps.note: Livy's story of Rome's beginnings, from Romulus to the Gauls, full of the legends Romans told about themselves.

steps.title: The Aeneid
steps.note: Virgil's epic of Aeneas, the Trojan who fled to Italy, and Rome's answer to Homer.

steps.title: Metamorphoses
steps.note: Ovid's book of transformations, and the source of most of the myths we know.

steps.title: Moral Letters To Lucilius
steps.note: Seneca's letters on how to live and how to face death, short enough to read one a day.

steps.title: Meditations
steps.note: An emperor's private notes to himself. Best read slowly, a few pages at a time.

steps.title: City Of God
steps.note: Augustine's answer to the sack of Rome in 410. Long, so many readers choose selections.

steps.title: The Decline And Fall Of The Roman Empire
steps.note: Gibbon's great history of how it all came apart, in famously elegant English.

extra.label: Timeline: the Roman Republic and Empire
Infographic: City of God on One Page

paths.title: Myths and Legends
paths.blurb: Gods and heroes from Greece to the North, then on into the legends of King Arthur.

steps.title: A Treasury Of Greek Mythology
steps.note: Start with the Greek myths themselves, retold for easy reading.

steps.title: Metamorphoses
steps.note: Then read many of the same stories as Ovid told them.

steps.title: A Treasury Of Norse Mythology
steps.note: Odin, Thor, Loki and the end of the world.

steps.title: Irish Mythology And Fairy Tales
steps.note: The heroes and the fairy folk of Ireland.

steps.title: Beowulf
steps.note: The Old English poem of a hero, a monster, the monster's mother and a dragon.

steps.title: The Story Of King Arthur And His Knights
steps.note: Howard Pyle's lively retelling, a good way into the Arthurian world.

steps.title: The Song Of Roland
steps.note: Charlemagne's rearguard holds the pass at Roncevaux: the great epic of medieval France.

steps.title: Sir Gawain And The Green Knight
steps.note: The finest of the medieval Arthurian poems, here in Tolkien's translation.

steps.title: Idylls Of The King
steps.note: Tennyson's Victorian Arthur, in verse.

paths.title: Faith and Reason
paths.blurb: Christian thought from Augustine to C. S. Lewis, with the great poems along the way.

steps.title: The Holy Bible
steps.note: Where everything else on this path begins. The Gospels are a good place to start.

steps.title: Confessions
steps.note: Augustine's own story of his search for God: the first great autobiography.

steps.title: City Of God
steps.note: Augustine on the two cities, the earthly and the heavenly.

steps.title: The Consolation Of Philosophy
steps.note: Written in a prison cell: Lady Philosophy teaches Boethius why fortune cannot touch what matters most.

steps.title: The Divine Comedy
steps.note: Dante's journey through Hell and Purgatory to Paradise.

steps.title: Paradise Lost
steps.note: Milton's epic of the fall of Satan and of Adam and Eve.

steps.title: The Pilgrims Progress
steps.note: Bunyan's allegory of the Christian life as a journey.

steps.title: Orthodoxy
steps.note: Chesterton explains, with great good humour, how he came to believe.

steps.title: The Everlasting Man
steps.note: Chesterton again, on human history and the place of Christ in it.

steps.title: Mere Christianity
steps.note: C. S. Lewis's wartime radio talks on what Christians have always believed.

steps.title: The Screwtape Letters
steps.note: Letters from a senior devil to his nephew: Lewis's sharpest and funniest book.

steps.title: Out Of The Silent Planet
steps.note: The first of Lewis's Space Trilogy, followed by Perelandra and That Hideous Strength: the same ideas, told as science fiction.

extra.label: Infographic: Four Bets on the Afterlife
Gospel reader in Greek and Latin

paths.title: Learning Latin
paths.blurb: From your first noun to reading real Latin, with the site's own tools alongside.

steps.title: Wheelocks Latin
steps.note: The standard course: forty chapters, each with readings from real Roman authors.

steps.title: Workbook For Wheelocks Latin
steps.note: Exercises to go with each chapter.

steps.title: Allen And Greenoughs New Latin Grammar
steps.note: The reference grammar to keep beside you.

steps.title: Cassells Latin Dictionary
steps.note: A good desk dictionary, Latin to English and English to Latin.

steps.title: Wheelocks Latin Reader
steps.note: Your first longer passages of real Latin, with notes.

steps.title: Winnie Ille Pu
steps.note: A treat: Winnie-the-Pooh in Latin.

paths.title: Gothic and Strange
paths.blurb: Monsters, doubles and haunted minds, from Mary Shelley to Oscar Wilde.

steps.title: Frankenstein
steps.note: Often called the first science-fiction novel, begun when Mary Shelley was eighteen.

steps.title: Complete Tales And Poems Of Edgar Allan Poe
steps.note: Start with The Tell-Tale Heart and The Fall of the House of Usher.

steps.title: Dr Jekyll And Mr Hyde
steps.note: Short enough to read in an evening, and better if you can forget you know the twist.

steps.title: The Picture Of Dorian Gray
steps.note: A portrait that ages so its owner does not.

steps.title: Dracula
steps.note: Told in letters and diaries, which makes it feel surprisingly modern.

paths.title: The Russian Giants
paths.blurb: The great nineteenth-century novels, then the Soviet century that followed.

steps.title: Crime And Punishment
steps.note: A murder, and what it does to the murderer. The best first Dostoevsky.

steps.title: Notes From Underground
steps.note: Short, bitter and funny: the voice of the underground man opens the door to all of Dostoevsky's great novels.

steps.title: Anna Karenina
steps.note: Tolstoy's novel of love, marriage and society.

steps.title: Chekhov Plays
steps.note: The great plays, from The Seagull to The Cherry Orchard.

steps.title: The Death Of Ivan Ilyich
steps.note: A judge faces death and asks whether he has lived well. Tolstoy's most perfect short work.

steps.title: The Idiot
steps.note: A truly good man, Prince Myshkin, among the greedy and the passionate of St Petersburg.

steps.title: Demons
steps.note: A comic and terrifying novel about a small town taken over by revolutionaries.

steps.title: The Brothers Karamazov
steps.note: Dostoevsky's last and greatest novel: three brothers, a murdered father, and the question of God.

steps.title: War And Peace
steps.note: Napoleon's invasion of Russia and five families caught up in it. Keep the who's who handy.

steps.title: The Master And Margarita
steps.note: The Devil visits Soviet Moscow, in a comic novel that could not be published in Bulgakov's lifetime.

steps.title: The Gulag Archipelago
steps.note: Solzhenitsyn's history of the Soviet prison camps, from the inside.
